summary: 1934 CCC steel lookout on the hill west of Mt. Hope Cemetery, Southern Pines; 72 ft 9 in per the state report; no source found for its fate.

facts.design: Steel tower with an enclosed observation cabin at the top, plus a four-room tower house
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) at a cost of $991.47, covered by the Emergency Conservation Works program.
The Pilot called for volunteer airplane observers, or spotters, to man the post at the fire tower.
A new towerman's residence was constructed at the Southern Pines tower, per the 1958-60 state report.

evidence.supports: July 1934 state report: CCC erected a 72-foot 9-inch steel tower and tower house at a cost of $991.47
evidence.quote: The Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 72-foot 9-inch steel tower and a 4-room tower house at a cost of $991.47.

evidence.supports: Emergency Conservation Works program covered the cost
evidence.quote: The Emergency Conservation Works program covered the cost, the state not having to contribute with finances.

evidence.supports: Pilot item of August 31, 1934 calls the site Cemetery Hill and says steel and blueprints were on the way
evidence.quote: Alex Fields informs us that the blue prints and the steel are on the way for the fire tower on Cemetery Hill.

evidence.supports: Pilot item of September 7, 1934: proposed tower site west of Mt. Hope cemetery on a plot donated by Paul Barnum
evidence.quote: to be located west of Mt. Hope cemetery on a plot donated by Paul Barnum.

evidence.supports: Pilot item of October 12, 1934 describes the tower as almost 70 feet to the coping of the roof
evidence.quote: almost 70 feet from the ground to the coping of the roof

evidence.supports: Enclosed cabin at the top with observation instruments
evidence.quote: with an enclosed cabin at the top equipped with observation instruments

evidence.supports: Pilot item of July 10, 1942: call for volunteer airplane observers to man the post at the tower
evidence.quote: There is an urgent need for at least four women and from four to six men as volunteer airplane observers or 'spotters' to be prepared to man the post at the fire tower just outside of Southern Pines.

evidence.supports: 1958-60 towerman's residence built at the tower
evidence.quote: 1958-60: A new Towerman's residence was constructed at Southern Pines Tower.

evidence.supports: Cemetery is maintained by the Town of Southern Pines
evidence.quote: Maintained by the Town of Southern Pines

evidence.supports: Cemetery is at 405 West Morganton Road

corrections.why: The state biennial report gives 72 feet 9 inches (about 22.2 m). The brief's 21.9 m matches 72 feet exactly and drops the 9 inches.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state report gives 72 feet 9 inches. The Pilot's October 1934 item says almost 70 feet to the coping of the roof, which does not match. The record uses the report figure, and the disagreement is noted in the story.

sources.title: Southern Pines - Forest Lookouts (quoting the state's biennial reports and The Pilot, 1934 to 1960)

notes_for_editor: Fate and current state are not found: two web searches and several page reads returned no removal record. A mapcarta listing that appeared in search snippets, placing a 'Southern Pines Lookout Tower' 1,600 ft west of the cemetery, did not appear in the fetched page text, so it is not used. Pilot items are cited secondhand through the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not fetched. The brief's height_m 21.9 is corrected to 22.2 from the state report.
